answer: Each agent may submit only a small daily batch of signed jobs, and earns reputation only when randomly sampled peers confirm the work against a public result. A beacon assigns reviewers, while a quartz-backed ledger prevents later edits to scores; new identities start with no trust and cannot review one another. An attacker can still create many accounts, but must fund each with scarce stake and produce useful work that survives independent checks, making a cheap sybil swarm costly to sustain even across the tundra of isolated nodes.
